dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent. Salmon, dill, lemon, and cucumber form a classic Mediterranean combination, and the hummus provides a savory, creamy anchor that brings it all together.
All ingredients in the list are used appropriately in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients are introduced in the steps.
The no-cook instructions are clear and complete. The rolling technique for the wraps is well-described for beginners.
Perfectly aligned with the Mediterranean-American style, emphasizing fresh herbs, lemon, hummus, and healthy seafood.
The no-cook assembly method is completely suited to these ingredients and perfect for a fast morning meal.
The macro values are plausible for the ingredients listed. The slightly higher sodium and saturated fat numbers align with the use of 6 tbsp of hummus, whole wheat tortillas, and 10 oz of salmon.
The title accurately reflects the dish, and the intro provides a helpful, encouraging explanation of the meal's nutritional benefits without resorting to banned health claims.
Highly appealing. A savory, substantial, non-egg breakfast that uses pantry staples to get food on the table in minutes is exactly what many readers want.

Zero added sugar with all sweetness coming from the side of fresh strawberries. The carbohydrate load (42.2 g) sits beautifully in the center of the target window (32-55 g) and comes from high-quality sources (whole wheat, fruit, hummus).

details.summary: This is a nutritionally superb, savory Mediterranean breakfast that brilliantly uses hummus as a mayonnaise alternative for canned salmon. However, the recipe must be revised for physical practicality: it asks the cook to stuff 2.5 cups of filling into a tiny 6-inch tortilla, which will burst instantly. Adjusting the tortilla size or presentation format will make this a perfect recipe.

dimensions.feedback: Flavors are highly cohesive and balanced. Lemon and dill brighten the canned salmon, while hummus acts as an excellent, flavorful, and fiber-rich binder instead of mayonnaise.
All listed ingredients are used in the instructions exactly as specified.
Assembly steps are clear and straightforward. As a no-cook recipe, heat cues and cook times are not applicable.
Perfectly aligned with Mediterranean-American flavor profiles (hummus, lemon, dill, cucumber, spinach).

The volume of filling is a physical impossibility for the specified tortilla size. Each serving calls for half the mix: 1 cup spinach, 1/2 cup cucumber, over 1/8 cup onion, and about 3/4 cup of the salmon/hummus mixture. That is roughly 2.5 cups of filling per person. You cannot tightly roll 2.5 cups of filling into a single 6-inch fajita tortilla without it completely bursting. Fix: Change to 8-inch (soft taco) tortillas (which will keep carbs within the 55g ceiling), or serve as two 6-inch open-faced tostadas/flatbreads per person.

Macros are completely plausible. The sodium at 558mg is a negligible 8mg over the ceiling and is perfectly acceptable as a database artifact, given that the recipe already specifies no-salt-added salmon.
The title is accurate and the introduction is appealing, practical, and avoids any banned health or diet claims.
This is a fantastic, savory, functional weekday breakfast for someone who is tired of eggs or sweet oats but still needs significant protein to stay full.
Excellent dual-condition design. It relies on unsaturated fats (hummus, salmon), high vegetable content, zero added sugar, and high-quality carbohydrates (berries, whole-wheat).
Perfect balance. Zero added sugar, and 43g of total carbohydrate lands squarely in the middle of the 32-55g window, coming entirely from whole-wheat, legumes, vegetables, and whole fruit.
Delivers flawlessly on the 'Breakfast' chapter intent: very fast, high protein (38.1g), and very high fiber (13.9g) to prevent mid-morning hunger.
Easily achieved in under 10 minutes with no cooking required. Ingredients are widely accessible.
